presentation.label: PIPO LOOP
presentation.summary: LOP gets a third value, PIPO: the sample's loop plays forward, then backward, and so on (ping-pong). ON stays the stock forward loop.
presentation.overview: Pipo Loop adds PIPO to the SAMPLE page's LOP parameter, after OFF and ON. A sample whose LOP is PIPO plays from STA to END, then back to STA, then forward again, for as long as the note lasts, with no jump at the turns. LOP's switch becomes a three-position switch like BD CLASSIC's WAV: OFF on the left, ON in the middle, PIPO on the right. PIPO is an ordinary LOP value: it saves with the sound and kit, takes parameter locks and scene locks, and comes back after a power cycle. A sound saved with PIPO plays as a normal forward loop (ON) on an OS without the mod. The turn falls on the audio engine's 32-frame block, so it comes up to about one block before STA or END.
highlights: Ping-pong loops for any sample, from the SAMPLE page's own LOP knob.
Lock PIPO on a step, or put it in a scene, like any LOP value.
No jump at the turns; ON and OFF stay stock.
Saved with the sound; plays as a forward loop on stock OS.
usage: On the SAMPLE page, turn LOP past ON to PIPO and play the sound: the loop between STA and END goes back and forth.
Set STA and END around a sustained part of the sample (a pad, a vowel, a held note) for a seamless back-and-forth drone.
Hold a trig in GRID RECORDING and turn LOP to PIPO to ping-pong only on that step; the other steps keep the sound's ON or OFF.

access.location: SAMPLE page, LOP (encoder G): OFF, ON, PIPO.
steps: Select a track whose sound plays a sample, and press SAMPLE.
Turn LOP (encoder G) clockwise past ON: the value reads PIPO.

controls.name: LOP
controls.doc: SAMPLE page, encoder G. OFF and ON as stock; PIPO plays the loop between STA and END forward, then backward, and so on. Locks per step and per scene. Drawn as stock's three-position switch, as BD CLASSIC's WAV: OFF left, ON middle, PIPO right.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.3.
Not yet run on a unit: tested in rytm-emu only.

A turn falls on a 32-frame audio block, up to about one block (plus 8 frames) before STA or END, so a PIPO loop is a few frames shorter at each end than ON's; inaudible on most material, audible on very short loops.
MIDI CC 30 (LOP) writes its value unchanged, as on stock: CC value 2 now gives PIPO, every other nonzero value ON. Other OFF/ON parameters still read ON for 2.
On stock OS, or a build without this mod, PIPO plays as ON.
LOP's switch is drawn with the knob in the middle for ON, where stock draws it on the right; the value text still reads ON.

claims: ui:SAMPLE page LOP value PIPO and its three-position switch
param:LOP range OFF/ON/PIPO, its value text and icon

load.display: About 0.1 % of an audio block with no sample looping, about 0.6 % with eight voices in PIPO (static estimate)
load.conditions: Static count of the compiled handler, run once an audio block before the sample engine: about 15 instructions for a voice with LOP OFF or no track, about 70 for one looping with ON, about 105 for one in PIPO, plus four 32-bit divisions for a voice whose STA, END or sample just changed. With the Rytm guide's 0.023 % of a block per instruction a frame: about 0.1 % with nothing looping and about 0.6 % with all eight voices in PIPO. Not measured on a unit.

tests.summary: rytm-emu c5732f0, OS 1.74, build PP06 (core-ar2 0.3 + 0.1.0), ramp sample on BD: LOP steps OFF/ON/PIPO on a three-position switch like BD CLASSIC's WAV; ON plays stock's loop, PIPO a click-free triangle at TUN about -24, 0 and +24; ON to PIPO mid-note; p-lock and scene lock; two voices; retrig; power-off persistence; stock 1.74 plays a saved PIPO as a normal loop. Not run on a unit.
